styles.label: Art
styles.blurb: Rijksmuseum, Van Gogh and the canal-side galleries.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Anne Frank House, canal ring and the old centre.

styles.label: Budget
styles.blurb: Free ferries, market food and cheap bike days.

stays.why: Walk to Dam Square, the Anne Frank House and Centraal station. Busiest and priciest, but you save on transit.
Quiet canals, small galleries and cafés. Ten minutes on foot to the centre and the Anne Frank House.
Local feel, Albert Cuyp market and lots of food. Near the Museumplein for the big art museums.
Good value and a short tram ride to the centre. Popular with locals and repeat visitors.

food: Try Dutch snacks: bitterballen, raw herring from a stall, and stroopwafels fresh off the iron.
Albert Cuyp market in De Pijp is good for cheap eats; check opening hours on the day.
Indonesian rijsttafel is a Dutch classic; book ahead for dinner.
Cheap lunch: broodjes (sandwiches) and soup in cafés, roughly EUR 8–15.
Tap water is safe to drink. Carry a bottle and refill it.
more_time: Swap a city day for Haarlem: a short train ride, with a pretty centre and the Frans Hals museum. Check times and fares on the day.
Take the free ferry behind Centraal station to Amsterdam Noord for a different, quieter side of the city.
Rent a bike for a half day and ride the canals and the Vondelpark. Follow local rules and park only in marked spots.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the Rijksmuseum, Van Gogh and the Anne Frank House; add a night for the Jordaan and a bike ride.

month_notes: January: cold and wet, highs near 7°C. Pack a warm waterproof coat and plan museum days.
February: still cold, around 8°C, with about 13 rain days. Indoor sights are the safe bet.
March: slowly warming to about 10°C. Expect showers; bring layers.
April: milder at around 13°C, but rain is still common. Good for walking between showers.
May: pleasant at about 17°C. A good month for canals and parks.
June: mild and bright, highs near 21°C. Busy season starts; book museums ahead.
July: warmest month, about 22°C, but about 15 rain days. Carry a light rain jacket.
August: similar to July, around 22°C with frequent showers. Peak crowds.
September: still mild at about 19°C. Fewer crowds than summer.
October: cooling to about 15°C with around 15 rain days. Bring a waterproof.
November: cool and wet, highs near 10°C. Short days; plan indoor sights.
December: cold at about 8°C with about 15 rain days. Dark early; dress warm and waterproof.

climate_guide.summary: Temperate and changeable: mild summers, cool winters, and rain in every month. Always carry a light waterproof.

items.title: Rain all year
items.text: Expect 12–15 rain days every month. Showers pass quickly, so a light rain jacket beats an umbrella in wind.

items.title: Mild summers
items.text: July and August peak around 22°C with lows near 14–15°C. Rarely hot; evenings stay cool.

items.title: Cool winters
items.text: December to February highs sit near 7–8°C and lows near 2–4°C. A warm coat, hat and gloves help.

items.title: Best months: May to September
items.text: Warmest and brightest, around 17–22°C. Also the busiest, so book museums and stays early.

items.title: Wind and changeable skies
items.text: Weather shifts within a day. Check the forecast each morning and keep plans flexible.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers, a waterproof jacket, comfortable walking shoes and a small day bag. Add a warm layer for winter.

transit.best: Walk or bike in the centre; use trams for longer hops.

modes.text: The main way around, run by GVB. Most routes run about 06:00 to midnight. Tap a contactless bank card (OVpay) or use an OV-chipkaart.
Fills the gaps where trams don't go. Same GVB tickets and OVpay tap-in.
Covers areas beyond the tram lines. A few night buses run after midnight.
Uber and Bolt work in Amsterdam. Taxis are metered and pricey; use them for late nights or heavy bags.
Not worth it in the compact centre. Parking is limited and costly; stick to trams, bikes and walking.
The centre is flat and compact, so walking is often fastest. Watch for bike lanes.
Locals' favourite. Rent for a half day and follow the rules: use bike lanes and park only in marked spots.
Free ferries cross the IJ behind Centraal station. A cheap way to see Amsterdam Noord.
